$comment: Known cross-hub ownership disputes the reach check may pass over.
Each entry pins the phrase, the hub that declares it, and the hub that currently
wins it. Both sides are required on purpose: an allowlist that only names the
phrase would swallow the next regression on that phrase too, and the whole reason
this check exists is that a broad pass hid 155 broken phrases behind a green run.
If a different hub starts winning an allowed phrase, that is new and it fails.
Every entry needs a reason and a review date. An entry nobody can justify on
re-read is an entry that should be a fix instead.

entries.reason: sk-design declares this exactly and still loses to a hub that declares nothing matching. Not resolvable by vocabulary; belongs to the lexical-lane work.
Same shape as 'design review': exact declaration, no matching declaration on the winner.

entries.phrase: design review of this slide deck
entries.reason: Same, and the winning hub has no slide-deck capability at all.
A 0.003 margin, and iteration is deep-loop's defining property. Same shape.
The winner declares nothing matching, so there is nothing to yield.
Awaiting an operator ruling: 'request a review' is deep-loop's command surface, 'review this request' is sk-code's. Both defensible.
Not a defect. A command surface winning a phrase that names that command is correct routing.
Two senses: authoring a skill package is sk-doc's, coding inside one is sk-code's. The bare phrase names neither act; a prompt with an authoring verb reaches sk-doc.
Same shape as 'opencode skill': authoring the agent file versus coding against the runtime.
Same shape as 'opencode skill': authoring the command file versus coding against the runtime.
Authoring a Claude Code agent file is sk-doc's; dispatching work to the Claude Code CLI is cli-external-orchestration's. The bare phrase reads as either.
A release-readiness playbook is sk-doc's; a release-readiness review loop is system-deep-loop's. Both are legitimate owners of the bare phrase.
A decision branch in a diagram is sk-design's; the word 'branch' pulls the bare phrase to sk-git. Not resolvable by vocabulary; belongs to the lexical-lane work, like 'design review'.
